fixes.explanation: That's the reason in verse 2: “…because the LORD’s time of release has been proclaimed.” No loophole, no mood swing, no lawyer in a fancy hat. The lender lets it go because the LORD called the time. I've been left in a drawer for years and never once got a notice that nice. Release means release, friend.

Bow is a fair guess, because people do bow to whoever's in charge. But the verse goes the other way. It says Israel will “…rule over many nations but be ruled by none.” Nobody bowing in that promise, baker. Israel isn't the one on the floor, and the blank wants rule.

That's it, baker. Verse 8 says, “Instead, you are to open your hand to him and freely loan him whatever he needs.” Think about a fist. You can't hold anything out with a fist, and you can't take anything either. An open hand can do both. And I'll say it again, because it's the word that does the work: freely.

Nothing in verse 15 mentions the nations watching. Moses is the one speaking here, and he says, “Remember that you were slaves in the land of Egypt, and the LORD your God redeemed you; that is why I am giving you this command today.” The reason isn't about who might be looking. It's about what Israel remembers about itself.
